On this page

Availability Results Component ​

The AvailabilityResults Livewire component handles displaying the results of an availability search and lets the user start the checkout process. This page explains how to use it and how to provide extra functionality.

UPGRADING FROM v5

The "advanced availability" props on this component have been renamed in v6 to match the new collection-scoped Rates system. If you passed advanced or :overrideProperties, or copied the advanced sub-view, see Breaking changes from v5 below.

Component basics ​

This component is designed to work for a single Entry. If you want to display availability for many entries at once, see the Availability Collection component, or for a cart-based multi-rate / multi-date flow see Cart booking.

In its most basic form, you can include it in your templates like so:

antlers
{{ livewire:availability-results :entry="id" }}

This will load the component and display the results for the Entry at the current page. As described in the Availability Search for a Single Entry page, you usually want to attach an instance of the AvailabilitySearch component so that the user can change their search:

antlers
<div class="max-w-md">
    <div class="my-8">
        {{ livewire:availability-search enableQuantity="true" calendar="range" }}
    </div>
    <div class="my-8">
        {{ livewire:availability-results :entry="id" }}
    </div>
</div>

Component properties ​

Of course, there are quite a few properties that you can set depending on the use case. Here's a list of all the available properties:

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
entrystringnone - requiredNeeds to be a Statamic Entry ID. The ID of the entry you want to display results for.
extraDaysinteger0When set to a number greater than 0, the component will also get availability for the days before and after the current period the user searches for.
extraDaysOffsetinteger0If extra days are enabled you can set an offset between the dates it searches for.
ratesbooleanfalseWhen true, resolves the per-entry rate labels. If the search was made for any rate (rate=any), every available rate is listed with its own price and "Book now" button.
rateSortingstring"order"Controls how the rate rows are ordered when listing all rates. Use "order" for each rate's configured order, or "price" to list the cheapest rate first.
showExtrasboolean or arrayfalseIf you want to display an Extras select box here, you can set this to true to show all extras or an array of the IDs you want to display. (more information below)
showOptionsboolean or arrayfalseIf you want to display an Options select box here, you can set this to true to show all options for this Entry or an array of the IDs you want to display. (more information below)
overrideRatesarray[]Override the resolved rate_id => label map with your own labels.
viewstring"availability-results"You can override the view that is used to render the component. Expects a name.blade.php file in the /resources/views/vendor/statamic-resrv/livewire folder.

Working with rates ​

When an Entry has more than one rate (for example different room types or fare classes), set rates="true" so the component resolves each rate's label and price:

antlers
{{ livewire:availability-search :rates="true" :any-rate="true" }}
{{ livewire:availability-results :entry="id" :rates="true" }}

When the search was made for any rate, every available rate is rendered as its own row, and the visitor picks one before booking. The order of those rows is controlled by rateSorting: "order" (the default) follows each rate's configured order, while "price" lists the cheapest first:

antlers
{{ livewire:availability-results :entry="id" :rates="true" rateSorting="price" }}

The rates sub-view ​

The list of rate rows is rendered by an anonymous Blade component, <x-resrv::availability-results-advanced>, found at availability-results-advanced.blade.php. The main view invokes it like this:

blade
<x-resrv::availability-results-advanced
    :$availability
    :entryRates="$this->entryRates"
    :dateStart="$data->dates['date_start'] ?? null" />

It loops the available rates, looks up each label with entryRates, shows the price and an optional cancellation-policy label, and books a specific rate via wire:click="checkoutRate('{rateId}')".

INFO

The filename still carries the word "advanced", but everything user-facing is now "rates": the prop is entryRates and the booking action is checkoutRate.

Cancellation policy ​

Each available rate row carries a cancellation_policy payload (a ['policy', 'period'] array) inside its data. When a rate has a policy configured, the component renders a customer-facing label:

  • Non-refundable for non-refundable rates.
  • Free cancellation until <date> for rates with a free-cancellation window (the date is the check-in date minus the rate's free-cancellation period).

Rates that inherit the global default with no period configured render no label at all. See Rates for how to set a per-rate cancellation policy.

Customizing ​

Obviously, depending on the use case, you'll need to customize the component to fit your needs. The main template file can be found at /resources/views/vendor/statamic-resrv/livewire/availability-results.blade.php. There you can select what elements you want to display and customize them.

Extras and Options (Optional) ​

Besides just displaying the availability results, you can also display the Extras and Options of that Entry. It might strike you as weird that this is part of the AvailabilityResults component instead of the AvailabilitySearch component, but the Extras and Options need access to the Entry data, so they need to be displayed in the same component.

By default, the Extras and Options are not displayed since they are part of the Checkout component. However there are cases where you might want to display them next to the availability results.

To do so, just enable the appropriate properties. For example:

antlers
{{ livewire:availability-results :entry="id" showExtras="true" }}

Checking out ​

The final task of the AvailabilityResults component is to let the user start the checkout process. When the user clicks "Book now", the component will create a "Pending" reservation and move the user to the checkout page.

Read along to learn more about the Checkout component.

Breaking changes from v5 ​

The "advanced availability" concept has been replaced by collection-scoped Rates. On this component that means a few renames you must apply when upgrading:

v5v6
advanced proprates prop
overrideProperties propoverrideRates prop
advancedProperties() computedentryRates() computed
checkoutProperty()checkoutRate()

The rate rows are now rendered by the anonymous <x-resrv::availability-results-advanced> component instead of a partial view. If you copied the old advanced sub-view, move your customizations to that component. See Upgrading to v6 for the full upgrade guide.

Related components ​

  • Availability List: list upcoming available dates for a single entry.
  • Availability Collection: show availability for many entries at once.
  • Cart booking: let visitors accumulate multiple rates and dates into one reservation.
